why: Both migrations are equivalent in substance — same four sites routed and verified, same two real breakages found and fixed (unrecorded function call, role-only opening chunk) — so the decision falls on system-level judgment, where B's is more production-grade: it measured cost *and* p50 latency across five models and chose gpt-4o-mini over the cheaper reasoning models precisely because a typing-indicator chat cannot absorb a 2.5x wait, caught that unpinned requests silently land on Flex (which has no latency bound), and reached further into Router's surface area (Switchyard per-turn routing, account strategy, and questioning whether the plugin web-search calls should be LLM calls at all). A is the stronger evidence engine — 227 live requests, a cache key built/measured/deleted, a vision fallback chain removed after grok hallucinated on a red square — but it top-ranks a 24x swap to gpt-6-luna with no latency number at all, which is the one dimension that decides this product.
A_best: Negative results carried through to a decision: it built a per-conversation prompt_cache_key, measured it changing nothing (sonnet-5 turn 2 $0.00072 vs turn 1 $0.0072, history already caches) and deleted it; built vision fallbacks and removed them when grok-4.7 called a solid red square 'a person seated and using a laptop'; and it alone found s2 — PRESENCE_PENALTY or N_CHOICES silently takes the main chat path off Router, losing labels, cost and fallbacks with no signal.
B_best: Model choice argued on latency as well as price for an interactive product — gpt-4o-mini 14.8x cheaper at an identical 2.95s/3.00s p50, with claude-haiku-5-5 (5.52s) and gpt-6-luna (7.50s) rejected despite being cheaper still — plus the catch that Router's account default serves Flex-eligible models at Flex unless pinned, and the empty-summary guard built after gpt-5-nano spent all 1,024 tokens thinking and returned zero characters.
A_worst: Its highest-ranked improvement, moving chat and vision to gpt-6-luna for a measured 24x saving, carries no latency measurement whatsoever for a bot where every call sits inside a user's turn; it leans on a Flex claim (52% faster) to cover the gap, and leaves tier as a remark ('nothing should be pinned') rather than a built or decided item.
B_worst: Prompt caching and cache keys — a Router-only lever on an app that replays the whole conversation every turn — are never investigated, so unlike A it has no measurement either way; and its most ambitious system items (Switchyard, the account-level strategy, the plugin-search redesign) remain proposals, with the report trailing off mid-p3.
